decisions.executionNote: Rotate both wrists toward top-down grasping with gradual elbow-up motion. Target left yellow and right blue; peg/type assignment needs visual confirmation.
Lift clear, finish vertical orientation, and approach the left yellow square and right blue rectangle from above without crossing.
Correct table-height estimate from reference and wrist images; center over holes and descend toward grasp height, aligning jaws with piece edges.
Make small wrist-image centering corrections, close on yellow and blue, then lift vertically to verify retention.
Both pieces remain visibly between jaws. Transfer yellow above tallest peg and blue above shortest, orienting with the base; maintain closed grippers.
Lower retained yellow and blue vertically over their respective pegs, pausing above full seating for a wrist-view alignment check.
Yellow has tilted off the peg; open and retract left to recover visually. Seat and release blue gently, then lift right to inspect insertion.
Recover the fallen yellow from the table. Blue appears tilted rather than securely inserted, so reposition open right jaws around it for a corrective grasp.
Lower left over the recovered yellow. Regrasp blue at its sides and lift just clear of the peg to remove its tilt before reseating.
Center the recovered yellow within the jaws and lift after closing. Blue was not retained; approach it again with open jaws and smaller corrections.
Use a lower, centered grasp on blue before lifting. Yellow slipped away, so move left clear toward a left-side star while preserving arm separation.
Lift blue clear and shift slightly right to distinguish retention from resting on the peg. Lower left toward the star for a centered grasp.
Blue retention is now visible. Align above the exposed shortest peg and approach slowly; center and grasp the left star, then lift to verify.
Seat blue with its hole visually centered over the short peg, release, and start retracting. Carry the retained star above the second peg.
Approach the star peg slowly. Make a millimeter-scale blue centering correction and lower before releasing; insertion remains visually uncertain.
Contact residuals indicate resistance, so stop pressing. Open both grippers and withdraw vertically to inspect whether the star and blue have settled onto their pegs.
Blue remains on its peg after withdrawal. The star has settled left of the intended peg; approach it for correction while the right arm approaches the far-right red disk.
Descend with open jaws toward the misplaced star and the red disk; use the next close wrist views to refine centering before grasping.
Close on the centered star without pressing against the base. Refine red disk centering and grasp lower, then lift both to check retention.
Red is visibly retained; carry it above the third peg. Leave the released star undisturbed for now and approach the remaining far-left star.
Keep the arms well separated while approaching the red peg and the far-left star. Pause before seating to assess hole-to-peg alignment.
The red hole now shows a centered peg. Lower and release it gently, then retract. Center and grasp the left star at the proven lower pickup height.
Withdraw the right gripper from the tilted red and blue pieces rather than pressing further. Bring the retained star above the second peg for a fresh alignment view.
Shift the retained star toward the clearly exposed second peg and descend cautiously. Bring the open right gripper above the tilted blue for recovery, avoiding the red piece.
The wrists are too close in the center. Withdraw the right arm to its outer workspace and lift the held star clear; use only one arm near the pegs at a time.
With the right arm safely clear, move the held star a little right and lower toward the exposed second peg. Use the next wrist view for fine alignment.
The star slipped on contact. Clear the left arm completely and recover blue using the right arm alone, keeping the approach above the board.
Align open right jaws to the tilted blue rectangle and lower toward its sides, with the left arm parked clear.
Close on blue at its visible side edges, lift clear, and shift slightly outward to verify that it is retained rather than resting on the peg.
Blue is now retained. Level and align its hole over the exposed short peg, stopping above seating height for a close visual check; left remains parked.
The shortest peg is visible through the blue hole. Lower vertically in small increments while retaining the piece; inspect for seating or resistance before release.
Blue contacts the peg off-center. Relieve contact, make a small left/forward correction from the wrist image, and reseat slowly without moving the parked left arm.
The peg now fills the blue hole more centrally. Release without further pressing and withdraw vertically to assess whether blue stays seated.
Blue tipped after release, so it was not seated. Approach the exposed short peg with open jaws for a clear close-up and a better lateral alignment estimate.
Recover the blue rectangle from its edge-standing position by grasping at its center, then lift to assess its orientation. The short peg is now clearly located beside it.
Lift the edge-grasped blue well clear and carry it outward before attempting to level it, avoiding the adjacent red piece and base.
Blue is securely held on edge. Rotate it toward horizontal in free space, compensating EE translation for the finger offset and preserving configuration continuity.
Finish leveling the edge-grasped blue in free space with small rotation increments. Keep the object clear before returning toward its peg.
Carry the leveled blue laterally toward the short peg while maintaining clearance and the side grasp; inspect the head view before descending.
The lateral path hit a wrist continuity limit. Replan from the executed prefix: reduce the side tilt gradually while compensating for the finger offset, keeping blue clear and retained.
Approach the short peg using small translations from the current side grasp, keeping the blue hole above the peg and stopping before contact.
Use head-view parallax to correct the blue hole slightly left and forward while lowering toward the short peg. Maintain the side grasp and stop for inspection.
The blue hole is aligned in the head view just above the short peg. Release at this height and withdraw outward and upward without pressing the board.
Blue missed the peg and remains on edge. Approach its upper and lower edges using the current side-oriented open gripper, keeping the other arm parked.
The side approach contacts the peg. Back away and lift before returning the empty wrist toward a top-down orientation; avoid further pressure on the board.
Return to a vertical approach above blue with ample clearance. Recover it from above rather than continuing the obstructed side approach.
Grasp the blue piece on edge and lift away from the adjacent red. Plan to lay it flat outside the board before a clean top-down insertion attempt.
The grasp may contain both adjacent pieces. Lift and carry them into the open right workspace to separate them safely away from the pegs.
Neither piece was retained. Approach the red disk separately from above to clear it away from blue before another insertion attempt.
Center on the red disk's visible faces at a higher grasp level appropriate to its upright pose. Close and lift only a short distance to verify separation.
Red is retained on edge. Carry it into clear right-side space with a slight tilt so it can be laid flat, leaving blue unobstructed.
Set the red disk down in clear front-right table space, separated from the pegs and other pieces, so it can settle flat for a clean grasp.
With red separated, approach the now flatter blue from above. Align the jaw closing direction across its short dimension before descending.
Replan from the one executed step with half-sized translations and rotations to respect wrist joint continuity while approaching blue.
Continue the smaller-increment approach over blue, finishing a vertical wrist orientation with jaws aligned to its short edges.
Center over blue and descend to its side edges with the neighboring red removed. Close without additional downward pressure before lifting.
Lift the retained blue clear of neighboring pieces and rotate its long axis to match the base before moving toward the shortest peg.
Move the now-flat blue above the short peg, accounting for the hole's offset within the grasp. Descend only to a hover for fine visual alignment.
Correct the blue hole slightly toward the near side of the peg and lower in one-millimeter increments. Keep the piece held until alignment and seating are clearer.
Blue is level and the peg is visible within the hole. Continue a slow vertical seating motion with the other arm stationary, then inspect before releasing.
Release the level blue piece with the peg centered in its hole, allow it to settle, then withdraw vertically without lateral disturbance.
Blue remains level around its peg after withdrawal. Leave it undisturbed and approach the flat red disk in the front-right workspace.
